M01.title: Read a story aloud to baby
steps: Sit comfortably, one hand on your belly.
Read slowly, with expression — your voice is the gift.
End with the same goodnight line each time.
M01.note: Babies hear from about 19–24 weeks and can come to know familiar voices. This is about familiarity and closeness, not making a baby ‘smarter’.

M02.title: Talk to your baby
steps: Tell baby about your day — what you saw, smelled, ate.
Use baby’s nickname.
Pause, breathe, and notice how you feel.
M02.note: Your voice is the clearest sound in the womb; newborns prefer their mother’s voice.

M03.title: Sing a lullaby
steps: Choose one lullaby (pages 22–23) or a family favourite.
Sing softly, as many times as you like.
Keep the same song for the coming weeks.
M03.note: Newborns show memory for sounds heard before birth; singing may also help bonding.

M04.title: Same story, same song
steps: Pick ONE short story and ONE song.
Read and sing them every evening from now until birth.
After birth, use them to soothe — they may sound familiar.
M04.note: In studies, newborns recognised passages and melodies heard often before birth.

M05.title: Calm music break
steps: Choose soft music you enjoy (instrumental, bhajan, raga, lullaby).
Lie on your side or sit propped up.
Let your breath slow with the music.
M05.stop: Keep volume comfortable; never place headphones on the belly.
M05.note: Music lowered anxiety in pregnancy trials; effects are modest.

M06.title: Soft Oṃ chanting
steps: Sit tall, shoulders soft. Breathe in through the nose.
Breathe out slowly: ‘aaa-uuu-mmm’, letting the ‘mmm’ hum.
Repeat 5–9 times; then sit quietly for a minute.
M06.stop: No breath-holding; use a soft voice; stop if dizzy.
M06.note: Slow, long exhalations are linked with calm; chanting studies are small.

M07.title: Gāyatrī mantra
steps: Read the meaning first (page 20).
Recite slowly 3 or 9 times, or listen to it.
Reflect: ‘May my mind be bright and kind.’
M07.stop: Some families follow initiation customs — follow yours, or choose another prayer.
M07.note: Heritage prayer (Ṛgveda 3.62.10); mantra practice may calm the mind — studies are weak.

M08.title: A Śānti (peace) mantra
steps: Choose Saha nāvavatu, Asato mā or Pūrṇamadaḥ (pages 20–21).
Recite slowly, ending with ‘śāntiḥ’ three times.
Rest your hands on your belly and feel the stillness.
M08.note: Peace prayers from the Upaniṣads; calm comes mostly from slow, steady breath.

M09.title: Madālasā’s lullaby
steps: Read the verse and its meaning (page 21).
Sing or speak it softly to baby.
Write one quality you wish for your child.
M09.note: A lullaby of wisdom from the Purāṇic tradition — shared here as heritage.

M10.title: Lullaby in your mother tongue
steps: Choose a lullaby in your home language (pages 22–23).
Ask an elder how they sang it.
Sing it to baby — the melody of your language is a welcome.
M10.note: Newborns are already tuned to the sound patterns of the language they heard in the womb.

M11.title: Indian story time
steps: Read one of the stories on pages 24–25 aloud.
Use different voices for the characters.
Talk about the story’s kindness or courage.
M11.note: Reading aloud = your voice for baby. The story’s values are for the family to share.

M12.title: Wisdom line of the week
steps: Read this week’s line and its meaning.
Write it on a card and keep it where you can see it.
Return to it when the day feels heavy.
M12.note: Contemplative reading from India’s philosophical texts.

M13.title: Sound bath
steps: Make a playlist on page 72: rain, birds, flute, veena.
Lie on your side with a pillow between your knees.
Listen without doing anything else.
M13.note: Listening to calming sound can reduce anxiety; evidence is modest.

M14.title: Baby-talk moment
steps: Say hello to baby by name.
Describe what you are doing right now.
Say: ‘I am here. I love you.’
M14.note: Small, frequent moments of voice and attention add up.

B01.title: Natural belly breathing
steps: Sit or lie on your side; hand on your belly.
Breathe in gently through the nose; feel the belly rise.
Breathe out a little longer than you breathe in (e.g., 4 in, 6 out).
B01.stop: Stop if dizzy, tingly or breathless.
B01.note: Slow breathing is a well-established relaxation skill taught in antenatal classes.

B02.title: Anulom vilom — no holding
steps: Right thumb rests by the right nostril, ring finger by the left.
Breathe in left, out right; in right, out left — slowly.
No pausing or holding the breath. 5–9 rounds.
B02.stop: Never hold the breath. Skip if your nose is blocked. Stop if dizzy.
B02.note: Gentle yogic breathing; small studies suggest calming effects.

B03.title: Bhrāmarī — humming bee
steps: Sit comfortably; close your eyes.
Breathe in through the nose; breathe out humming softly ‘mmm’.
Optional: fingers lightly over the ears. 5–7 rounds.
B03.stop: No breath-holding; don’t press the ears; stop if dizzy.
B03.note: Humming lengthens the out-breath; research is early and small.

B04.title: Śītalī — cooling breath
steps: Curl the tongue (or rest it behind the teeth).
Breathe in slowly through the mouth; breathe out through the nose.
5 rounds, only if comfortable.
B04.stop: Skip if you have asthma, a cold, low blood pressure or sensitive teeth. No holding.
B04.note: A traditional cooling breath; little research — use only if it feels pleasant.

B05.title: Daily walk
steps: Walk at a pace where you can still talk.
Build slowly towards 150 minutes a week.
Walk in cooler hours; carry water.
B05.stop: Stop with any warning sign (bleeding, pain, dizziness, fluid, contractions).
B05.note: WHO and ACOG recommend regular moderate activity for most pregnancies.

B06.title: Pelvic-floor squeezes
steps: Gently squeeze as if stopping wind and urine; lift up and in.
Hold 3–5 seconds while breathing normally; release fully.
Repeat 8–10 times, 3 times a day.
B06.stop: Don’t practise while passing urine. Stop if painful.
B06.note: Strong evidence: reduces leaking urine late in pregnancy and after birth.

B07.title: Neck & shoulder release
steps: Sit tall. Slowly tilt the right ear to the right shoulder; 3 breaths.
Repeat on the left. Roll shoulders back 5 times.
Interlace fingers, stretch arms forward, round the upper back gently.
B07.stop: Move slowly; stop with pain or numbness.

B08.title: Cat–cow (Mārjārī)
steps: On hands and knees; padding under the knees.
Breathe in: gently lift the chest and look ahead.
Breathe out: round the upper back softly. 6–8 rounds.
B08.stop: Keep the movement small; no deep sagging of the back. Stop with pain.
B08.note: Among postures shown to be well tolerated in late pregnancy.

B09.title: Supported butterfly
steps: Sit on a folded blanket; soles of feet together.
Cushions under the knees; spine tall.
Breathe slowly for 1–2 minutes. No bouncing.
B09.stop: Skip if you have pelvic (pubic) pain.
B09.note: A common, gentle hip-opener in prenatal yoga programmes.

B10.title: Mountain & side stretch
steps: Stand feet hip-width; chair beside you.
Breathe in, raise one arm; breathe out, lean gently to the side.
3 breaths each side.
B10.stop: Hold a chair if unsteady. Stop if dizzy.
B10.note: Standing stretches were well tolerated in studies.

B11.title: Wall pelvic tilts
steps: Stand with your back against a wall, knees soft.
Breathe out: gently press the low back towards the wall.
Breathe in: release. 8–10 times.
B11.note: Simple back care used widely in antenatal classes.

B12.title: Side-lying rest
steps: Lie on your left or right side.
Pillow between the knees, one under the belly, one under the head.
Relax the jaw, hands and feet with each out-breath.
B12.stop: After the first trimester, avoid lying flat on your back.
B12.note: Side-lying avoids pressure on major blood vessels; relaxation lowers stress.

B13.title: Ankle circles & calf stretch
steps: Seated: circle each ankle 10 times each way.
Standing at a wall: step one foot back, heel down, 3 breaths.
Swap legs.
B13.stop: One-sided calf pain or swelling: call your doctor at once.
B13.note: Gentle movement for circulation and comfort.

B14.title: Tree pose at the wall
steps: Stand side-on to a wall, one hand on it.
Rest the other foot on your ankle or calf (never the knee).
3–5 breaths; swap sides.
B14.stop: Always use the wall. Skip if balance feels unsure.
B14.note: Balance work with support; falls are the main risk, so the wall is essential.

B15.title: Gentle warrior II
steps: Wide, comfortable stance; front knee over the ankle.
Arms out to the sides; gaze over the front hand.
3 breaths; swap. Keep a chair nearby.
B15.stop: Short stance, no strain; stop with pelvic pain.
B15.note: Well tolerated in a study of 26 postures.

B16.title: Open seated twist
steps: Sit sideways on a chair.
Turn the chest gently towards the chair back — away from the belly.
3 breaths each side; twist from the upper back only.
B16.stop: No deep or closed twists. Skip if uncomfortable.
B16.note: Gentle mobility; deep twists are avoided in pregnancy.

B17.title: Guided relaxation (yoga nidrā)
steps: Lie on your side, well supported.
Move attention slowly: feet, legs, hips, belly, hands, face.
Rest in stillness; rise slowly via your side.
B17.stop: Never flat on your back after the first trimester.
B17.note: Guided relaxation lowered perceived stress in an Indian trial.

B18.title: Partner foot & hand massage
steps: Partner uses plain oil or lotion.
Slow, gentle strokes on hands and feet.
Talk, listen to music, or sit in silence together.
B18.stop: No strong essential oils; skip a swollen or painful calf.
B18.note: Small studies link massage with lower anxiety.

H01.title: Letter to baby
steps: Begin: ‘Dear little one…’
Write what you are feeling and hoping.
Keep the letters together for your child.
H01.note: Writing about feelings can ease stress; it also deepens connection.

H02.title: Three good things
steps: Write three good things from today, however small.
Add why each one happened.
Read them aloud to baby.
H02.note: Gratitude exercises have small positive effects on wellbeing.

H03.title: Worry to wish
steps: Write one worry in a single line.
Below it, write the wish hidden inside it.
Choose one small step towards the wish (or someone to ask).
H03.note: ‘When troubled by thoughts, cultivate the opposite’ — Yoga Sūtra 2.33.

H04.title: Partner’s voice for baby
steps: Partner sits close and talks or reads to the bump.
Use a regular time — e.g., after dinner.
Partner can sing the family lullaby too.
H04.note: Babies hear voices outside the womb from mid-pregnancy.

H05.title: Partner task of the week
steps: Partner chooses and completes this week’s task.
Mother ticks it off — and says thank you.
Talk about how support feels.
H05.note: Practical and emotional support protects a mother’s wellbeing.

H06.title: Record a voice message
steps: Record a message or lullaby on your phone.
Log it on page 73.
Play it for baby after birth.

H07.title: A family blessing
steps: Ask an elder for a blessing (āśīrvāda) for you and baby.
Write it on page 75.
Say thank you with a hug or namaste.
H07.note: Blessings by elders are a heart of Indian pregnancy celebrations.

H08.title: Belly-touch hello
steps: Rest both hands on your belly.
Stroke slowly in circles; say hello.
Notice any movement in reply.
H08.note: In a small study, babies moved more when mothers touched their belly.

H09.title: Reach out
steps: Call or meet someone who makes you feel safe.
Share one joy and one worry.
Ask for one specific help, if you need it.
H09.note: Support from others protects mothers’ mental health.

H10.title: Imagine meeting baby
steps: Close your eyes; breathe slowly.
Imagine holding your baby — warm, safe, calm.
Write one sentence about what you saw.
H10.note: Thinking about baby is linked with bonding after birth.

S01.title: Mandala colouring
steps: Choose 2–3 calm colours.
Colour from the centre outwards, slowly.
Notice your breath as you work.
S01.note: Structured colouring reduced anxiety in small studies.

S02.title: Soft gaze at a yantra
steps: Place the yantra (page 17) at eye level, arm’s length.
Look softly at the centre dot (bindu); blink freely.
Close your eyes and rest. 1–3 minutes.
S02.stop: Blink normally; stop if your eyes strain or water.
S02.note: A contemplative heritage practice — not a medical treatment.

S03.title: Trace the Śrī Yantra
steps: Trace the nine triangles slowly with a pencil.
Colour the petals, starting from the outside.
End by resting your gaze at the centre.
S03.note: Sacred geometry of the Śrī Vidyā tradition; shared as heritage art.

S04.title: Kolam on dots
steps: Use the dot grid on page 18.
Draw one continuous line around the dots.
Let mistakes be part of the pattern.
S04.note: Threshold art drawn at dawn across South India.

S05.title: Mudrā & breath
steps: Choose a mudrā from page 15.
Rest the hands on your thighs or belly.
Breathe slowly for 2 minutes.
S05.note: Hand gestures from ritual, dance and meditation; healing claims are unproven.

S06.title: One calm minute
steps: Set a 1-minute timer.
Notice 3 sounds, 2 sensations, 1 breath.
Smile at baby before you get up.
S06.note: Short mindfulness pauses; pregnancy research is encouraging but mixed.

S07.title: Cakra check-in
steps: Use the map on page 14.
Ask: where do I feel tense, warm, open?
Say the affirmation for that place.
S07.note: A symbolic map from the tantric tradition — not anatomy or medicine.

S08.title: Five-layer check-in (Pañca Kośa)
steps: Body: what does it need? Breath: is it easy?
Mind: what am I feeling? Wisdom: what do I know?
Joy: what made me smile?
S08.note: The five sheaths of the Taittirīya Upaniṣad, used as a gentle self-care list.

S09.title: Lotus visualisation
steps: Close your eyes; imagine a lotus on still water.
With each out-breath, one petal opens.
Rest in the open flower.
S09.note: Guided imagery may ease anxiety; studies are small.

S10.title: Kind wishes (maitrī)
steps: Silently wish: ‘May I be well. May my baby be well.’
Widen to family, friends, all beings.
Rest in the warmth.
S10.note: Loving-kindness practice raises positive feelings; Yoga Sūtra 1.33.

S11.title: Draw your own mandala
steps: Start with a dot and a circle (page 70).
Repeat one shape around the circle.
Add rings until it feels complete.
S11.note: Creative, repetitive drawing can be calming.

S12.title: Moon gazing
steps: Find the moon tonight from a safe, comfortable spot.
Note its shape on the moon tracker.
Breathe slowly and tell baby what you see.
S12.stop: Stay in safe, familiar places after dark.
S12.note: Mindful moments in nature support calm.

N01.title: Folate foods
N01.note: Folate helps form the baby’s brain and spine. Take folic acid tablets as your doctor prescribes.

N02.title: Iron + vitamin C
N02.note: Iron builds blood for two; vitamin C helps absorb it.

N03.title: Iodised salt
N03.note: Iodine is essential for the baby’s thyroid and brain.

N04.title: Choline foods
N04.note: Choline supports brain development; a small trial found benefits from higher intake.

N05.title: Omega-3 fats
N05.note: Omega-3 fats lower the risk of early birth and build brain and eyes.

N06.title: Protein at every meal
N06.note: Needs rise in the 2nd and 3rd trimesters.

N07.title: Calcium foods
N07.note: For baby’s bones and teeth, and your own.

N08.title: Water & fluids
N08.note: Helps with constipation, swelling and urine infections.

N09.title: Food safety
N09.note: Prevents infections that can harm pregnancy.

N11.title: Mindful meal
N11.note: Eating slowly helps you notice hunger and fullness.

N13.title: Vitamin B12
N13.note: Important for the nervous system; vegetarians can run low.

N14.title: Less caffeine
N14.note: Keep caffeine under 200 mg a day.

N15.title: Tastes of home
N15.note: Flavours reach the amniotic fluid; babies may later accept familiar tastes more easily.

X01.title: Hum one comfortable note
steps: Breathe in through the nose.
Breathe out humming one easy note until the breath is gently done.
Repeat 5–9 times.
X01.note: Humming slows the breath — the same calming mechanism as chanting.

X02.title: A favourite poem, slowly
steps: Choose a short poem or prayer you love.
Read it aloud slowly, three times.
Notice one line that stays with you.
X02.note: Slow, rhythmic recitation steadies the breath.

X03.title: Words of peace
steps: Choose a peaceful verse from your own tradition — or ‘May we be safe, may we be well’.
Say it slowly three times.
Rest your hands on your belly.
X03.note: Repetition with slow breath can calm the mind.

X04.title: A family lullaby
steps: Ask an elder for a lullaby from your family.
Write the words on page 73.
Sing it to baby.
X04.note: Babies can remember melodies heard often before birth.

X05.title: Thought for the week
steps: Read this week’s line.
Write it on a card where you will see it.
Return to it when the day feels heavy.
X05.note: A reflection habit to steady the mind.

X06.title: Counted breathing
steps: Breathe in through the nose for 4.
Breathe out softly for 6.
Repeat 8–10 times; no holding.
X06.note: Slow, longer exhalations help the body relax.

X07.title: Lullaby humming
steps: Breathe in through the nose.
Hum a lullaby tune on the out-breath.
5–7 rounds.

X08.title: Cool-cloth breathing
steps: Place a cool damp cloth on the back of your neck.
Breathe slowly through the nose.
Sip cool water.
X08.note: Simple cooling and slow breath on hot days.

X09.title: Body-scan relaxation
steps: Lie on your side, well supported.
Move attention slowly from feet to face.
Rest; rise slowly via your side.
X09.stop: Avoid lying flat on your back after the first trimester.

X10.title: Family wishes
steps: Ask family members for one wish for baby.
Write them on page 75.
Read them aloud to the bump.
X10.note: Feeling surrounded by support helps mothers thrive.

X11.title: Soft gaze at a pattern
steps: Place a flower or geometric pattern at arm’s length.
Rest your eyes on its centre; blink freely.
Close your eyes and rest.
X11.note: A simple focusing exercise for calm attention.

X12.title: Geometry colouring
steps: Choose the triangles pattern on page 17.
Colour slowly from the outside in.
Notice your breath as you work.

X13.title: Hands-on-belly breath
steps: Rest both hands on your belly.
Breathe slowly for 2 minutes.
Feel the rise and fall.

X14.title: Head-to-toe feelings check
steps: Scan from head to toe: tense, warm, easy?
Name the feeling in one word.
Breathe into the tense place three times.
X14.note: Naming feelings can make them easier to hold.

X15.title: Five-question check-in
steps: What does my body need? Is my breath easy?
What am I feeling? What do I know?
What made me smile today?
